reason: The text introduces Job as a member of the elite (wealthy, influential, described as 'great among all the people of the East') and portrays him extremely favorably. He is characterized as 'blameless, upright, God-fearing, and turning away from evil' (תָּם וְיָשָׁר וִירֵא אֱלֹהִים וְסָר מֵרָע). Even when calamities befall him, he is portrayed with integrity—tearing his robe, shaving his head, worshiping God, and the text explicitly states 'in all this Job did not sin, nor did he charge God with wrong' (בְּכָל־ זֹאת לֹא־ חָטָא אִיּוֹב). The portrait of this elite figure is one of moral and spiritual excellence, not unfavorable portrayal.
